ai.summary: npm-app/clean-package.js now writes a trailing newline to temp.package.json after JSON.stringify. Semistandard compliance fix for temp file output. Internal build script change.

eli5.text: When the build tool creates a temporary copy of the project's settings file to prepare it for publishing, it now adds a single empty line at the very end. This is purely a behind-the-scenes formatting step that makes the temporary file follow the team's coding style rules; it has no effect on the settings themselves or on anything you can see. The change is internal and already live, affecting only the way the build script writes that scratch file during the preparation process.

ai.title: Add confidence scoring to system prompt brainstorming
ai.summary: backend/src/system-prompt.ts updated to require explicit confidence scoring (0-100) within the <brainstorm> block. Logic gates file editing: scores <90 force user clarification, while >=90 permit plan selection and execution. This change restricts autonomous action on ambiguous requests.

eli5.text: The assistant now has to rate how confident it is that it understands your request before it tries to carry it out. After it lays out its plan, it gives itself a score from 0 to 100, and if that score is below 90, it will stop and ask you to clarify rather than guessing. So if you give it something vague or unclear, you will notice it asking follow-up questions instead of jumping straight to editing files.

ai.title: Run terminal commands from project root
ai.summary: handleRunTerminalCommand now prefixes commands with cd ${projectRoot} before execution. This ensures consistent working directory context for spawned processes. Import projectRoot from ./config in npm-app/src/tool-handlers.ts.

eli5.text: The assistant now starts every terminal command from the project's main folder, so commands that depend on relative paths or shared project files run consistently instead of from whatever folder the session happened to be in. If you watched it work, you wouldn't see extra typing, but any command relying on project-wide configuration or sibling files will find them reliably from the top level.

Nobody outside the publishing pipeline is affected, and the only visible effect is that the published listing now reports a new release number. This is standard behind-the-scenes housekeeping, not a new feature or capability.

ai.title: Fix project directory resolution and terminal cwd reset
ai.summary: Refactored `projectRoot` from a static `config.ts` export to a dynamic `getProjectRoot()` function in `project-files.ts` to correctly resolve the working directory. Updated `chat-storage.ts`, `menu.ts`, and `tool-handlers.ts` to consume this new accessor, ensuring file operations and terminal commands target the initialized project root. The system prompt in `backend/src/system-prompt.ts` now explicitly states that the working directory resets to the project root for each command, aligning backend instructions with the frontend's `cd ${getProjectRoot()}` execution logic.

eli5.text: When you run commands through the assistant (like installing a package or checking git status), those commands now always start from the same correct project folder every single time, instead of sometimes starting from the wrong place. Previously, the project folder was determined once when the app started and stored in a fixed spot; now it's looked up freshly whenever it's needed, so commands and file operations always point to the right directory. If you watched the assistant run terminal commands, you'd notice they no longer fail or behave inconsistently just because the folder got confused about where it was.

ai.title: System prompt step 4 adds file context loop
ai.summary: Step 4 in backend/src/system-prompt.ts now instructs the agent to use update_file_context and return to step 1 when more files are needed. Blank line between 3a and 3b removed. Internal prompt logic only.

eli5.text: The assistant now has a built-in reminder to keep gathering files when it runs low on context, looping back to review files instead of guessing blindly. This tightens up an internal checklist so the assistant asks for clarification rather than muddling through with incomplete information.

ai.title: Improve terminal command timeout handling and status reporting
ai.summary: Refactored `handleRunTerminalCommand` to use dynamic timeout messaging and explicit status strings instead of boolean flags. `formatResult` now accepts an optional `status` parameter, allowing accurate reporting for both timeouts (`Command timed out after X seconds. Partial results shown.`) and normal completions (`Command completed`). This change affects `npm-app/src/tool-handlers.ts` and updates internal tracking in `musings.knowledge.md`.

eli5.text: When the tool runs a terminal command, it now provides clearer messages about whether the command finished normally or timed out. Previously it used a simple yes/no flag; now it gives a specific message like 'Command timed out after X seconds. Partial results shown.' or 'Command completed'. This helps you see more accurately what happened when a command does not finish in the expected time, and it affects the internal tracking file that records these behaviors.

ai.title: Switch to uncertainty score
ai.summary: System prompt logic in backend/src/system-prompt.ts replaces confidence scoring with an uncertainty metric. Thresholds invert: proceed if uncertainty ≤ 10, halt for clarification if > 10. musings.knowledge.md marks related context and IP config tasks as resolved.

eli5.text: When you ask the assistant to do something, it now rates how unsure it is instead of how sure it is. If it feels more than a little uncertain (above 10 out of 100), it will pause and ask you to clarify before proceeding. This applies to the internal process the assistant uses to decide what to do next after reading your request.

ai.title: Lower system prompt uncertainty threshold to 5
ai.summary: The system prompt in `backend/src/system-prompt.ts` now triggers clarification requests when the uncertainty score exceeds 5, down from 10. This change tightens the threshold for proceeding without user confirmation, aiming to reduce ambiguity in plan selection. The update affects the core brainstorming logic for all agent sessions.

eli5.text: The system prompt now triggers clarification requests when the uncertainty score exceeds 5, down from 10. This change tightens the threshold for proceeding without user confirmation, aiming to reduce ambiguity in plan selection. All agent sessions will now be more conservative in their decision-making, asking for clarification earlier when there's any doubt about the user's intent.

ai.title: CLI menu becomes one-time print with colorized ASCII
ai.summary: Refactored `npm-app/src/cli.ts` to remove persistent menu state (`isInMenu`) in favor of a one-time print flag (`lastInputWasMenu`). `npm-app/src/menu.ts` updated to use `chalk` for random-colored block-character ASCII art and removed `console.clear()` calls in favor of `process.stdout.clearLine(0)`. Menu display now triggers once per ESC press without blocking subsequent input handling.

eli5.text: When you press the ESC key in the program, a colorful ASCII art menu now appears one time and then disappears, instead of staying open and blocking your other actions. The menu text is now displayed in random colors using block characters, and it no longer clears your entire screen. This makes the menu less intrusive, allowing you to continue typing or interacting with the program right after viewing the menu.

ai.title: Update system prompt structure and menu art
ai.summary: System prompt step 3 formatting flattened from sub-items 3a/3b to direct conditionals. CLI menu art replaced ASCII block letters with geometric shapes and added AI/CODE tags. Color randomization logic updated to select three distinct colors from a wider palette for menu rendering.

eli5.text: The text that appears when you open the program has been cleaned up so it reads more like plain directions instead of a numbered list with sub-letters, making it easier to follow when you ask the assistant a question. The colorful splash screen you see when you start the program now uses a few different colors picked at random from a bigger range, and the logo is drawn with simple shapes tagged 'AI' and 'CODE' instead of the old blocky text. These are small, behind-the-scenes tweaks that just freshen up how things look and read today.

ai.title: Bump manicode npm package version to 1.0.35
ai.summary: Version field in `npm-app/package.json` incremented from `1.0.34` to `1.0.35`. Internal release metadata update. No functional changes or new features.

eli5.text: The software's build number was silently incremented as part of routine maintenance, with no visible changes to how it works. If you use the AI coding assistant, you would notice nothing different today since this only updates internal release metadata rather than adding features or fixing issues.

ai.title: Add hardware fingerprint ID to npm-app client init
ai.summary: New `fingerprint.ts` derives a SHA-256 base64url ID from `systeminformation` (BIOS, baseboard, CPU, OS). `config.ts` exposes `initFingerprint` to populate `fingerprintId`; `index.ts` awaits this during `manicode` startup before `Client` instantiation. Scope limited to `npm-app` CLI; adds `systeminformation` and `@types/systeminformation` deps. Fingerprint computed asynchronously in parallel with project root init to mask latency.

eli5.text: When you start the assistant, it now quietly reads details about your computer's hardware, things like the make and model, processor, and operating system, and turns that into a unique, scrambled code. That code is sent along with your connection so the service can tell your machine apart from others. It only affects people using the internal command-line version of the assistant; regular users won't see anything different, but the startup might take a fraction of a second longer as it quietly gathers those hardware details in the background.
